newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end firmer, 30-year yield at new low.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end firmer, 30-year yield at new low.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Monday, sharply outperforming U.S. treasuries, with technical factors helping the Canadian 30-year long bond yield reach an all-time low, analysts said.

"There's no fundamental news whatsoever. This is all technically driven. We broke the old highs early this morning and we're sort of in uncharted waters right now," said Sheldon Dong, head of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn. "Anyone that follows charts had buy signals."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.60 to C$118.66 to yield 6.566 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 19/32 to yield of 6.58 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to a negative spread of one basis point from a positive spread of five basis points on Friday.
The Canadian 30-year long bond is now trading with its lowest yield since the issue was launched in December 1990.
Dealers said that once the long bond pushed through its all-time price high, it forced many traders to scramble to cover short positions, although volumes were not that heavy.

"With a market that had improved so much already, nobody wanted to be short," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc. "With fewer players around, the market can move very quickly either way."

In new issue news, the Canadian government on Monday said it planned a global offering of US$1.0 billion of five-year bonds to help refinance its foreign exchange reserves. Market sources said the global bond issue would be lauched tonight in Asian markets.
In economic news, the value of Canadian building permits issued in May fell 12.0 percent from April.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month fall of 0.1 percent in May. The data were positive for bonds but did not have a major impact on the market, analysts said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.85 to C$109.38 to yield 5.979 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which firmed 11/32 to yield 6.26 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 28 basis points from 21 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.06 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.08 percent.
